'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**Three [[Chinese people|Chinese]] nationals and two [[Mauritania]]ns are abducted at gunpoint from a construction site in Kwala, [[Mali]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/18/gunmen-kidnap-chinese-mauritanian-workers-in-central-mali (Al Jazeera)]
*Protests erupt across [[Iran]] as the country is facing its worst drought in 50 years. Two protestors are killed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/17/one-man-shot-dead-in-irans-khuzestan-water-crisis-protests (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 138 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 6,866. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/07/17/covid-19-record-high-of-138-fatalities-bring-death-toll-to-6866 (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
****[[Myanmar]] reports a record 233 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 4,769. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/myanmar-reports-233-new-deaths-from-covid-19-total-stands-at-476920210717225204 (ANI News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 10,082 new cases and 141 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, prompting the [[Government of Thailand|government]] to impose a nationwide ban on gatherings with a maximum penalty of a two-year jail term, a fine of up to 40,000 [[Thai baht|baht]] ([[United States Dollar|US]]$1,220.15) or both for violators. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/17/thailand-bans-gatherings-as-covid-cases-deaths-hit-new (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 3,718 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 47,904. [https://vietnamnews.vn/society/994581/viet-nam-records-3718-new-cases-of-covid-19-on-saturday.html (Viet Nam News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 54,674 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since mid-January. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-uk-records-54-674-new-coronavirus-cases-and-41-more-deaths-12357817 (Sky News)]
****[[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care]] [[Sajid Javid]] tests positive for COVID-19, despite having been fully vaccinated, one day after he met with [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-17/u-k-health-secretary-sajid-javid-tests-positive-for-covid-19 (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] imposes a night-time curfew from 1 a.m. to 6 a.m. and bans all music on the [[Islands of Greece|island]] of [[Mykonos]] in an effort to reduce the local spread of COVID-19. These restrictions would last until July 26. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/563533-greece-bans-music-on-mykonos-to-curb-covid-19-spread (''The Hill'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] reports a record 1,405 new cases and six deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of cases to 16,471 and the national total of deaths to 85. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/447056/covid-19-infections-and-deaths-soar-in-fiji (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 34 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.wftv.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-34-million-death-toll-nears-609000/EHDW4P334JEPFIXSP4RHX75JXE/ (WFTV)]
*[[Ghana]] culls more than 4,500 chickens and restricts the movement of poultry after nearly 6,000 birds died from the highly pathogenic [[H5N1]] [[avian flu]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ghana-culls-thousands-chickens-bans-poultry-movement-amid-avian-flu-outbreak-2021-07-17/ (Reuters)] 

'''International relations'''
*[[Japan–South Korea relations]]
**[[South Korea]] summons the [[Japan]]ese [[ambassador]] following remarks by a Japanese senior official mocking [[South Korean President]] [[Moon Jae-in]]. Moon had hinted at a summit with [[Japanese Prime Minister]] [[Yoshihide Suga]], to which the official responded that it was not a possibility and that Moon was "[[masturbating]]". South Korea states that the remarks were highly inappropriate, but the [[Government of Japan]] said that the remarks were not directed at Moon. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/south-korea-summons-japan-undiplomatic-inappropriate-remarks-15239336 (CNA)]
*[[2019 Bolivian political crisis]]
**At the request of [[Bolivia]], Argentine prosecutors file charges against former president [[Mauricio Macri]], security minister [[Patricia Bullrich]], defense minister [[Oscar Aguad]] and former Argentine ambassador to Bolivia [[Normando Álvarez García]] for allegedly supporting the removal of [[Evo Morales]] from power in November 2019. The [[Argentine government]] of that time is also accused of sending [[ammunition]] and weaponry to help the government of interim president [[Jeanine Áñez]] suppress protests organized by Morales' supporters. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/07/17/charges-filed-against-former-argentine-president-macri-for-helping-overthrow-evo-in-bolivia (MercoPress)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States civil unrest]], [[History of violence against LGBT people in the United States|Violence against LGBT people in the U.S.]]
**[[Los Angeles Police Department]] officers fire rubber bullets at close range as [[LGBT+]] activists showed up to counter far-right protesters who called for a boycott of Wi Spa which allows trans women to use women’s facilities.  Dozens of activists were arrested following the chaotic and sometimes violent encounter. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/video/2021/jul/18/police-fire-rubber-bullets-after-anti-trans-rights-protest-at-los-angeles-spa-turns-violent-video (''Guardian'')]
*A [[Nationals Park shooting|shooting]] at a baseball game in [[Washington, D.C.]] between the [[Washington Nationals]] and the [[San Diego Padres]] causes the game's suspension at the bottom of the sixth inning. Four people were shot just outside of the Third Base Exit at [[Nationals Park]]. [https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/31834736/washington-nationals-suspend-game-vs-padres-police-say-2-shot-stadium (ESPN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
**Over 100,000 people protest across [[France]] against [[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]]'s plan to require [[COVID-19]] vaccinations for health workers, along with other restrictions on unvaccinated citizens. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/french-protests-call-freedom-amid-government-vaccine-push-2021-07-17/ (Reuters)]
